item.title: Antarctica’s 2 native flowering plants responded differently to 7 years of warming
item.description: Research on King George Island examined how two native Antarctic plants responded to long-term warming. Antarctic hairgrass displayed reduced hydraulic conductivity and photosynthesis compared to those in natural conditions. In contrast, Antarctic pearlwort increased both its hydraulic conductivity and photosynthetic capacity. This study provided insights into contrasting adaptive strategies of these plants under sustained environmental changes. These findings highlight the need to understand species-specific responses to climate change effects. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: How farmers are helping reverse farmland wildlife decline
item.description: The resurgence of corn buntings and various wildlife species showcases the power of collaborative conservation work initiated by local farmers. item.title: Four North Carolina homes repaired after Helene face demolition after FEMA buyouts
item.description: In the aftermath of Hurricane Helene, four homes in the Cottages at Cypress Run neighborhood in Hendersonville face demolition due to severe flooding. Previously, these homes were repaired through homeowner efforts and community volunteerism. item.title: Queensland dairy farmer opened four campsites after drought forced her family to sell 40 cows
item.description: Agritourism is gaining momentum among Australian farmers struggling with drought-related financial pressures. Landowners like Libby Rough are transforming their properties into camping havens, creating alternative income streams. This shift not only aids in sustaining their farms during tough times but also promotes local agricultural education among visitors. Moreover, local authorities are streamlining regulations to encourage this thriving sector, enhancing community engagement with farming practices. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: When the atmosphere slows the Earth: Uncovering a subtle signal of climate change
item.description: Atmospheric circulation governs weather and climate, but it also carries angular momentum. When winds shift or mass redistributes, the atmosphere can exchange momentum with the solid Earth, slightly altering the planet's rotation rate. This is not a new concept, but what happens under long-term global warming? Fuente: Phys.org.

Throughout the decade, contractors will engage in tasks like invasive species control and planting native trees. After the project, the Southern Conservation Trust will ensure the area remains cared for and healthy. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: En 1974, Francia necesitaba evitar que París volviera a inundarse. La solución fue tan sencilla como radical: borrar tres pueblos del mapa
item.description: La gran inundación de París de 1910 dejó una imagen difícil de olvidar: calles convertidas en canales, vecinos desplazándose en barca y el Sena alcanzando 8,62 metros en el puente de Austerlitz. Francia necesitaba impedir que una crecida semejante volviera a golpear la capital y terminó adoptando una solución a una escala gigantesca. A unos 190 kilómetros de París construyó un depósito capaz de almacenar 350 millones de metros cúbicos de agua. El problema era que en el lugar elegido ya había algo: bosques, campos y tres pueblos enteros. Algo donde guardar agua. El problema no era únicamente… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: 57 new deep-sea species discovered in Argentina’s Mar del Plata Canyon, including ‘Loki’ sea cucumber
item.description: In a groundbreaking deep-sea voyage off Argentina, scientists uncovered 57 brand new marine species alongside five previously unclassified genera. Using a remotely operated vehicle, they pulled samples from the Mar del Plata Submarine Canyon. Among these marine marvels was a unique and translucent sea cucumber whimsically dubbed Loki. A subsequent collaborative workshop was instrumental in accelerating the species identification process, highlighting the astonishing biodiversity of the South Atlantic's deep ecosystems. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: The expansion of Heathrow would be an expensive disaster for Britain and the world. Burnham needs to block it | George Monbiot
item.description: A third runway would fly in the face of reason. If we are to prioritise human life over short-term ‘growth’, we need to use planes less, not more If a third runway is built at Heathrow, what will be the impact on the wealth of the nation? It will cost us somewhere between £23.4bn and £62.5bn. These are not my figures ; they weren’t calculated by environmental groups, but by the Department for Transport. For decades, government ministers have told us that airport expansion is essential for “growth”. item.title: Cien días después de los terremotos en Venezuela: la vida en medio del desplazamiento y la recuperación
item.description: «Yo estaba en un edificio que colapsó. Quedé bajo los escombros y pensaron que estaba muerta cuando me sacaron.
